newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach emergency rota for S.W.Trains.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach emergency rota for S.W.Trains.

text.p: Stagecoach's South West Trains passenger trains franchise said it was introducing an emergency timetable from Monday because of problems over driver shortages.

South West Trains, which was taken over by Stagecoach Plc a year ago, said it expected to cancel some 250 services next week following a productivity deal reached with its 750 drivers for 70 to take voluntary redundancy.
The company said it had underestimated the impact of taking drivers off duty for training on the new routes they would be driving.
Britain's government rail franchising office has approved South West Trains application to introduce a special timetable involving 39 cancellations a day from Monday.
It said this would allow the company to make timetable adjustments that would eventually benefit customers.

Stagecoach could face heavy penalties by the government's rail franchising authorities over the cancellations. South West Trains had already been cancelling an average of 17 trains a day over the last week.
South West Trains, which operates rail services from London to Southampton, Weymouth and Exeter, said the cancellations would help it produce a more reliable, although reduced timetable.
The pressure group Save Our Railways urged the Department of Transport to intervene.
Campaign coordinator Jonathan Bray said: "There are serious questions to be asked about why the contract was given to Stagecoach on the basis of cost-cutting plans which have proved unworkable."
